sentence: This project studies how a cancer-driving gene changes the metabolism of neuroblastoma tumors so they escape the immune system.
This project uses machine learning to sort children with status asthmaticus into groups and tests how magnesium and aminophylline work in each group.
This project studies how the nerve cells that control different tongue muscles differ in how they work and in their genes.
This project studies how one neuron uses opposing pathways to control food searching behavior.
This project offers sequencing and other tools that let cancer researchers study how genes are built and work.
This project builds a deep learning model that uses patient data and brain CT images to predict complications of traumatic brain injury.
This project studies how developing skin cells sense signals and rearrange their connections to form a layered epidermis.
This project builds a microscopy method that records the rapid activity of neurons in the olfactory bulb.
This project builds an algorithm that speeds up Pulsed Dipolar Electron Spin Resonance Spectroscopy by collecting only part of the data.
This project studies how coronaviruses spread between species in bats and other wildlife and what conditions allow this.
This project uses mass spectrometry to work out the structures of protein complexes made by HIV and its host cells.
This project manages and analyzes large datasets to understand the immune mechanisms of celiac disease using statistics and machine learning.
This project develops a technique that inserts large pieces of DNA into mouse chromosomes to make mouse models of cancer.
This project studies how a gene works in brain development and searches for other genes behind smooth brain in patients.
This project provides mouse genotyping, sperm cryopreservation and microscopy imaging support for researchers studying balance and hearing.
This project tries to find out which gut bacterial metabolites damage the intestine and cause inflammation in metabolic syndrome.
This project uses a sequencing method to detect treatment refractory stem cells of myelodysplastic syndromes months before relapse after transplant.
This project provides computing, bioinformatics and biostatistics support for research projects.
This project uses mass spectrometry to study proteins in animal models of alcohol drinking and dependence.
This project gets a high-throughput automated patch clamp system to study ion channels, which matter for the heart, brain and skeletal muscle.
